# SEO-117: Split sitemaps before the protocol size limits

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

No single sitemap file exceeds the protocol's maximum of 50000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed; larger inventories are divided into several files referenced from a sitemap index.

## Rationale

A file over either limit is rejected in full, so a growing site crosses the boundary silently and loses the whole submission at the moment the inventory is largest and the file matters most.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_sitemap"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Have the generator chunk its output on entry count and byte size rather than assuming the inventory stays small, and emit an index whenever more than one file results. Keep the index itself within the same limits.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Count the entries and measure the uncompressed byte length of every published sitemap file, including each child named by an index.
- Evidence: `SITEMAP`, `BUILD_OUTPUT`, `HTTP_HEADER`
- Automated check: `sitemap-size-limits`

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
